newsitem.title: UK: German shares hit 4th record, gold slumps.
newsitem.headline: German shares hit 4th record, gold slumps.

text.p: German shares stormed to their fourth record close in a row on Tuesday as a buoyant dollar boosted bond markets and French equities within sight of their historic high.

British stocks also overcame some of their interest rate jitters to recoup Monday's fall, aided by Wall Street's positive start and strong debt markets. The Dow was up 15 points after 40 minutes trade.
Gold, in contrast, slumped to fresh three year lows. It was fixed in the afternoon at $367.40, down from $369.00 at the morning fix.
Analysts forecast gold could weaken further as a strong dollar discouraged buyers and selling by gold mining houses cast a bearish pall over the market.

The dollar drifted off 23-month highs against the mark, French franc and Swiss franc in overnight dealings that followed comments by German and U.S. officials on the dollar's status as a reserve currency ahead of European monetary and economic union (EMU).

Foreign exchange markets were galvanised overnight by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing saying on Monday that investors might want to switch into dollars in the runup to the launch of a single European currency in 1999.

"The general trend of the dollar continuing to strengthen is in place...but we are going to have some further hiccups on the road to monetary union and at those times we may see the deutschemark strengthen," said David Brickman, European analyst at Yamaichi International.
By 1500 GMT, profit-taking had pushed the dollar down to 1.5641 marks and 113.73 yen against 1.5428 marks and 113.68 yen in late Europe on Monday.

On European stock markets, Germany's 30-share DAX index stormed to a fresh trading peak at the start of business and closed at its fourth closing record, up 28.38 points, or nearly one percent, at 2,886.98.
The dollar was the major support, but equities gained also from the record strength of German government bonds.
"Everybody who was in the market is happy and everybody else is being forced to pile in," said one trader. "Psychologically the DAX is already at 2,900 points."
Shares in chemical company BASF AG jumped 3.4 percent to end bourse dealings up 1.99 marks at 60 marks, while Bayer AG rose three percent to 64.55 marks.
In later screen-based, the IBIS DAX index was up 33.57 points at 2,887.03.
The dollar and strong bond markets were also behind a strong rally in French shares, which surged within a whisker of their February 1994 record of 2,360.98 before retreating a little.
By 1500 GMT the CAC-40 index was up just over 30 points, or 1.3 percent, at 2,348.

The dollar was the main cause of the bourse's rise, dealers said. Companies with U.S. units, heavy exports to the United States or those in competition with U.S. manufacturers were the biggest beneficiaries.
"The rise may look excessive but if you look at it objectively, Paris is lagging the other European markets, particularly Frankfurt, where the gap is 500 points," one trader said.
Leading British blue chips recouped Monday's losses, lifted by firm debt and FTSE futures markets and a positive outlook on Wall Street.

By 1500 GMT, the benchmark FTSE 100 index was up 21 points at 4,059, only 35 points off their November 26 record. But volumes remained light, despite the governemnt selling its remaining holdings in a series of utlities.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5641 marks and 113.73 yen against 1.5428 marks and 113.68 yen in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 21.3 points, or 0.53 percent, at 4,059.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 30.08 points, or 1.3 percent, at 2,348.71.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 28.38 points, or 0.99 percent, at 2,886.98.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $367.40, down from $369.00 in the morning and at a fresh three-year low. Silver was holding midday levels around $4.70.
